topic: Ubadari, CCUS & Compression (UCC) project FID and forward gas/CO2 development
wiki_text: On 22 November 2024 bp, on behalf of the Tangguh PSC partners, announced a final investment decision on the ~US$7 billion Tangguh Ubadari, CCUS, Compression (UCC) project. UCC develops the Ubadari gas field, adds onshore compression, and implements Indonesia's first at-scale carbon capture, utilisation and storage via enhanced gas recovery (targeting an estimated 15 million tonnes of CO2 sequestration in its initial phase). It is designated a national strategic project and aims to unlock an estimated 3 trillion cubic feet of additional gas to backfill the existing three Tangguh trains (combined ~11.4 mtpa). Ubadari first gas is targeted for 2028. Groundbreaking for the CCUS/Ubadari works was held in 2025. UCC is brownfield development to sustain Tangguh feedgas, not a new liquefaction train.

topic: Train F reactivation tied to Eni Geng North / North Ganal Block gas
wiki_text: Bontang's currently operating trains are G and H; Trains E and F are idle/on standby. Plans are underway to reactivate Train F to process up to ~1,200 mmscfd of gas from the Geng North-1 discovery in the North Ganal Block, operated by Eni, extending the plant's operating life. Reactivation had not been completed as of the research date, so Train F remains idled; the reactivation is a forward/recon-relevant development to monitor.

topic: Arun regas/LNG hub development: storage-expansion study and terminal-use agreements
wiki_text: Perta Arun Gas (Pertamina Gas subholding) continues to develop Arun (Lhokseumawe, Aceh) as a regasification and LNG hub near the Strait of Malacca. Pertagas and the Korea Maritime & Ocean University Consortium (KMOUC) completed a joint LNG storage-expansion study (conducted Oct 2024-Feb 2025) under a June 2024 MoU. TotalEnergies and Axpo have signed terminal-use arrangements for Arun storage tanks. These are hub/storage developments and terminal-use deals; the import regasification nameplate (~3 mtpa) is unchanged.
